scope.method: Read-only static application/platform/dependency-bytecode review. No source changes, builds, tests, provider mutations or device actions.

findings.title: Destination preflight accepts writable/deletable directories without create capability
findings.evidence: Explicit FLAG_DIR_SUPPORTS_CREATE inspection currently applies only to the owned-provider fallback. All other destinations pass when folder.isDirectory and folder.canWrite are true. The actual pinned androidx.documentfile1.0.1 canWrite bytecode returns true for flags&4 (SUPPORTS_DELETE), and separately flags&2 (SUPPORTS_WRITE), without requiring flags&8 (DIR_SUPPORTS_CREATE). Official AndroidX source confirms this behavior.
findings.trigger_and_impact: An external DocumentsProvider directory with a valid write URI grant and DELETE-only or WRITE-only capabilities passes preflight despite not supporting child creation. TransferProcessor then invokes the full transfer before OutputStore.save attempts createFile and fails. This unnecessarily downloads/caches potentially large media for a destination known in advance not to support creation.
findings.recommendation: Require a successful directory metadata query explicitly advertising FLAG_DIR_SUPPORTS_CREATE for all SAF destinations. Independently require the external write URI grant, retaining the same-UID exception needed on API29. Extend the existing owned-provider fixture/regression to cover delete-only and write-only flags and fail before a transfer begins.
findings.dependency_evidence: Cached actual pinned classes.jar inspected with javap; canWrite contains independent early-success checks for flags4,8 and2.
findings.status: Reported to parent; not edited by reviewer.

verified_observations: Both destination pickers obtain persisted read/write URI permission before adopting the selected tree. Queued tasks and batch drafts store destination snapshots; changing a later default does not silently redirect existing tasks.

The app intentionally retains old persisted grants when the default changes, preserving existing queued jobs and saved SAF documents. This is not treated as an unconditional permission leak without reference/usage evidence.

Preflight runs on Dispatchers.IO before transfer. SecurityException failures are classified as STORAGE_PERMISSION_DENIED; missing/offline provider state is not proof that its saved file entries should be erased.

Default Downloads publication uses MediaStore scoped rows with IS_PENDING before verification, then clears pending only at commit. Recovery filters exact app owner and expected Download/dosos73 directory.

SAF publication recovery validates same authority and exact directory membership of the recorded document ID, then verifies size/SHA256. Ambiguous or unverifiable results preserve the file for review rather than indiscriminately deleting it.

The same-UID API29 grant-lookup compatibility path still checks provider UID and declared creation capability; the finding concerns missing explicit creation checks in the ordinary external-provider path.
limitations: No real revoked grant, removable volume or third-party cloud provider was exercised. Runtime outcomes still need targeted tests.
An apparently writable provider can still reject a later operation or lose its grant; preflight cannot guarantee that future publication will succeed.
The exact pinned dependency bytecode was inspected, but no instrumented reproduction was run.
No second independent proven defect was identified. Grant-count garbage collection or a destination-repair UI was not invented as a mandatory feature in this review.
